findings.scenario: Segment is `interrupted` with write-once hashes H1/P1/E1/C1. A duplicate interrupt delivery CASes `active -> interrupted` or rewrites hashes to H2 (or any payload that does not equal the stored four hashes). Lines 488-490 require reject/replay-attach with zero mutation and say duplicate interrupt delivery cannot cancel. Lines 373-375 still list `any bound-hash mismatch` as a first-class `interrupted -> cancelled` trigger, so the same CAS can emit a terminal cancelled receipt and drop HITL without a unique accept/reject decision. That races the human decision and violates duplicate-delivery-only-attaches plus only-unique-decision-or-failed-live-gate-compare terminals.
findings.remediation: Delete `any bound-hash mismatch` from the `interrupted -> cancelled` allowed-transition bullet. Keep that bullet as rejection, expiry, revocation, or stale expected state. Leave hash mismatch as cancel only on a failed live-gate/hash compare while processing the unique `accept-proposal` decision (already at 491-493). Duplicate/self CASes and any rewrite of the four hashes must remain reject-or-attach with zero mutation.

audit.proof_assessment: HEAD equals BASE; only the existing S2 planning contract is in scope. The v4 Grok FINDINGS are prior evidence, not authority: finding 1 quotes a HITL ban on `retryable-failure` that is not in these bytes (current 358-362 and 517-518 require attempt 0 to CAS to terminal `failed`/`transient-retry-consumed` before index one is claimed, and HITL then evaluates the completed current attempt). Finding 2 is only half-closed: 488-493 splits duplicate attach from accept-path mismatch, but 373-375 still authorizes cancel on any bound-hash mismatch. Typed-proposal mutex (351-355) still blocks `active -> completed` without unique `accept-proposal`.
residual_risks: `active -> interrupted` is a multi-record CAS (segment, settled attempt, interrupt, proposal, expected state, held reservation) with no single closed transaction record; in-memory fixtures cannot prove durable atomicity.
RouteSegmentStateV1 has no decisionHash; unique `accept-proposal` uniqueness is deferred to the S3 slot CAS.
`interrupted -> completed` requires the reservation still held and never reconciles it, so accept can leak budget.
Kill-switch on or reservation loss during `interrupted` fails the accept live-gate but is not an independent `interrupted -> cancelled` trigger unless an accept is processed or expiry fires.
Line 484 leftover `Resume or cancellation` can be misread as `interrupted -> active` even though that transition is unlisted and the four hashes are forbidden outside `interrupted`.

Claim-index-one preconditions at 498-501 still describe attempt 0 as `retryable-failure` without restating the atomic terminalizing CAS; implementers must not treat that paragraph as a claim API separate from 517-518.
Acceptance criterion 8 does not mention retry-then-HITL or duplicate-interrupt attach, so AC-only tests can miss both.
